old_caption: The video captures a dynamic scene of a stormy sky, filled with dark, swirling clouds. The clouds are thick and heavy, with shades of gray and black dominating the frame, creating an ominous atmosphere. As the video progresses, the clouds begin to shift and move, revealing glimpses of lighter areas where the sky is slightly brighter. These lighter patches suggest the presence of rain or the breaking of the storm. The movement of the clouds is fluid and continuous, giving a sense of the storm's intensity and the passage of time. There are no visible objects, animals, or characters in the video; the focus remains solely on the dramatic sky. The camera appears to be stationary, allowing the viewer to fully absorb the evolving patterns and textures of the clouds. The overall effect is one of raw natural power and the unpredictable nature of weather systems.

caption: The video captures a dense field of dark storm clouds filling the entire frame, their billowing surfaces rendered in deep gray-blue tones. A faint brighter edge lingers near the lower-left corner, while the central and right portions stay dark between pulses of light. The cloud mass appears largely fixed in layout, with no obvious translation or deformation. The illumination glows diffusely from within the clouds rather than as a visible bolt crossing the sky. A soft glow swells in the lower-center and right regions, lighting surrounding cloud edges before receding into darkness. A brightening then flickers low in the center and fades, followed by another localized flare in the lower-central clouds that subsides. A more extensive illumination develops across the central mass, with strong light spreading around dark silhouettes before dimming. A faint brightening reappears in the lower-center and left, gradually softening as the ongoing sequence of dark cloud illumination continues.

An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.

collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.

camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.

processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.
